samples.question: This image shows six four-by-four grids, each drawn as an outlined box with thin internal grid lines. The single grid in the upper row is the reference grid. The five grids in the lower row are the candidates, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. In every one of the six grids exactly eight of the sixteen cells are filled solid, so all six grids carry the same number of filled cells and the same amount of ink. The reference grid is drawn slightly larger than the candidates, so only the pattern of filled cells matters, never a grid's size or its position on the canvas. Every grid is drawn upright in the same orientation, and no candidate is rotated or flipped. Exactly one candidate is the exact complement of the reference: comparing the two grids cell by cell at matching row and column positions, that candidate fills every cell the reference leaves empty and leaves empty every cell the reference fills, so laying it over the reference would cover the whole four-by-four square with no gap and no doubly covered cell. One of the other four candidates is an exact copy of the reference pattern, and each of the remaining three disagrees with the exact complement in at least two cells. Which numbered candidate is the exact complement of the reference grid? Answer with exactly one of: grid-1, grid-2, grid-3, grid-4, grid-5.
